issue_context.title: BUG: value_counts(observed=True) inconsistent between SeriesGroupBy and DataFrameGroupBy
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.

- [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the main branch of pandas.


### Reproducible Example

```python
>>> s = pd.Series(["a", "b", "c"], dtype="category").iloc[0:2]
>>> s
0    a
1    b
dtype: category
Categories (3, object): ['a', 'b', 'c']
>>> s.groupby(level=0).value_counts()
0  a    1
   b    0
   c    0
1  b    1
   a    0
   c    0
dtype: int64
>>> s.groupby(level=0, observed=True).value_counts()
0  a    1
   b    0
   c    0
1  b    1
   a    0
   c    0
dtype: int64
```


### Issue Description

The result contains `0` values for unused categories in each group with `observed=True` , unlike `DataFrameGroupBy`:
```python
>>> df = pd.DataFrame(s)
>>> df
	0
0	a
1	b
>>> df.groupby(level=0, observed=True).value_counts()
0  a    1
1  b    1
dtype: int64
```


### Expected Behavior

The behavior should be the same for `SeriesGroupBy` and `DataFrameGroupBy`. I am not sure what should be the expected behavior here. 

The `groupby` documentation specifies that `observed` parameter has effect on groupers. Considering `by` and `level` parameters are the groupers, it might make sense that in this case `GroupBy.value_counts` is not affected by the `observed` keyword and it follows the behavior of `Series.value_counts` which does keep unused categories. It would mean that `GroupBy.value_counts` (and probably `Series/DataFrame.value_counts` too) would require an additional `observed` parameter, like the suggestion in https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/43498.

On the other hand, if we consider that the `observed` parameter makes sense in this case, `SeriesGroupBy.value_counts(observed=True)` should not return `0` values for unused categories as for `DataFrameGroupBy`.

Related: performance issue on `GroupBy.value_counts` on categoricals [#46202](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/46202)

comments:
Thanks for opening this @LucasG0. I was incorrect in #46202; as you stated above, observed should only impact the groupers. Moreover, we should be consistent with `Series.value_counts` and `DataFrame.value_counts`:

```
s = pd.Series(["a", "b", "c"], dtype="category").iloc[0:2]
df = pd.DataFrame(s)
print(s.value_counts())
print(df.value_counts())
```

gives

```
a    1
b    1
c    0
dtype: int64
a    1
b    1
c    0
dtype: int64
```

Thus the `SeriesGroupBy.value_counts` behavior is correct here, the `DataFrameGroupBy.value_counts` has a bug.

review_comments:
It fixes an other bug related to `normalize` incorrectly producing NaN on non-observed categories:
```
>>> c1 = pd.Categorical(["a", "b"], categories=["a", "b", "c"])
>>> c2 = range(2)
>>> df = pd.DataFrame({"c1": c1, "c1": c2})
>>> df.groupby("c1").value_counts(normalize=True)
c1  c2
a   0     1.0
    1     0.0
b   1     1.0
    0     0.0
c   0     NaN    # <--- 0 is expected
    1     NaN    # <--- 0 is expected
dtype: float64
```
I guess these are by definition NaN here as we reindexed. this seems quite unfortunate as .value_counts() should be integer valued. can we fill on the reindex iteself? (which will keep the int dtype)

When normalize is True (this section of code), the values are percentages in [0.0, 0.1]. The nans don't come from a reindex, rather here they are coming from where `indexed_group_size = result_series.groupby(...).transform('sum')` is 0.
We're going from a single grouper to multiple groupers here; instead, can you add a multiple groupers case so as to have both?
Yes I'll restore the original single grouper test
@rhshadrach I added tests for the single grouper case. They actually tests when both groupers and non-groupers are categorical, as this path was not tested in the multiple groupers test.
what is the fill_value hitting? is there a test that needs this?

The purpose of `fill_value=0` is to fill non-observed categories count with 0 as they are not present in the `result_series`, and this behavior is tested in the added tests. Does it answer your question ?
I also tried to make this change directly in `_reindex_output` method, so it handles the fact that groupings might have a different observed attribute, but it breaks 60 tests.
Makes sense that reindex_output wouldn't work here; the schema for groupby.value_counts differs from other ops.

Does L1761 `observed=self.observed` actually do anything? I'd hazard a guess that the groupby code is just using the `observed=False` from L1752. If that is the case, can you make L1761 set observed to False as well for readability.
`observed=self.observed` is needed for categorical grouping columns. `observed=False` is used L1752 so every category of any categorical non-grouping column is included in the result.
Ah, thanks - I forgot the above groupers on L1752 are only the non-grouping columns.
Why is this test changing values? In particular the order.

I modified this test so it uses multiple groupers (`country` and `education` instead of `country` only), thus the second index level is the `education` column and is sorted by the groupby `sort=True` default behavior.

I will remove the `as_index` change.
It looks like you've added the single grouper test back but with changes - this makes the diff very hard to follow. Would it be an issue to restore the original test fully?

It just adds some slight redundancy with other single grouper tests. I restored the original test, now called `test_categorical_single_grouper_with_only_observed_categories`, with a small change to `observed=True` case regarding this fix
@LucasG0 - there is too much changing here. Correct me if I'm wrong, but it appears the original test is not restored - it seems to be heavily modified.

The original test on the main branch is called `test_categorical`, to be more explicit and to avoid confusion with other added tests, it is now called `test_categorical_single_grouper_with_only_observed_categories` ([link](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/46798/files#diff-94eb7e512970f337748151525e12830e7ca10c5e8acf4db15a00f56a9b2e6814R323)) and I added it in [this commit](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/46798/commits/fc8ea62187c89b8fd92aba071e54e378089edab4).

I slightly modified the original test in this PR to fix the expected behavior with `observed=True`. In the original test, the result would differ depending on `observed` while it should not - non grouping columns are not affected by `observed`, and grouping columns do not have non-observed values here, thus `observed` has no effect.
There are no NaN values though?
No, the filling value is 0 - if a key is not present, it appears 0 time.
